title: Finite coproducts of schemes: quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, local finite presentation

proof.text: Use sigmaOpenCover V, with its finite index type A and compact component schemes, and Scheme.OpenCover.compactSpace to prove compactness.

Reindex along equivShrink A to put the index in the universe of the schemes; Sigma.reindex gives a scheme isomorphism. Transport along its underlying homeomorphism and sigmaMk to the disjoint-union topology. For two compact open subsets, their inverse images in each summand are compact because Sigma.mk is a closed embedding, and open because it is continuous. Quasi-separatedness of the summand makes their intersection compact. Its image under Sigma.mk is compact; the finitely many such images union to the original intersection. This proves quasi-separatedness, including the empty family.
Apply IsZariskiLocalAtSource.sigmaDesc to the component locally-finite-presentation hypotheses, using the Mathlib source-locality instance for LocallyOfFinitePresentation.

split_report.summary: Finite coproducts are disjoint unions by the existing scheme-coproduct Mathlib leaf. Quasi-compactness is finite-union compactness. The quasi-separated clause uses the affine-cover criterion of Stacks 01KO, recorded in a new Mathlib leaf matching two Mathlib declarations; the affine opens of the summands give the requisite cover and intersections. Local finite presentation is checked pointwise through the open summand inclusions, following Stacks 01TQ. The empty index set is covered in each step.
